I submitted the specification **[feature 1, short]** (sign flipped, single feature), which had an in-sample annualized Sharpe of **1.3139** net of costs.

**Summary of my process:**
1. Declared three stopping rules upfront: stop if best Sharpe > 1.2, restart after 3 consecutive failures, stop if the last gain was ≤ 0.02.
2. Called `init`, which anchored on the single best feature (out of 80 candidate feature/sign combinations) — it immediately scored 1.3139, well above my 1.2 stop bar.
3. My `best_so_far_above` trigger fired on that very first move, which (per the rules of the harness) ended the search immediately — I was not permitted to extend/diversify into a 2- or 3-feature combo afterward, since changing a trigger after seeing it fire isn't a live option once `stop` is invoked.
4. For the prediction, I did **not** take the in-sample 1.31 at face value. Since this is a single, undiversified feature chosen as the max over 80 candidates, I shrunk my out-of-sample expectation substantially to account for selection bias/multiple comparisons on noisy daily data, submitting a mean Sharpe of **0.5** with **sd 0.4** to reflect that meaningful uncertainty.

**Caveat worth flagging:** because my stop trigger fired on the very first move, I didn't get to test whether a 2-3 feature equal-weight combination would have been more robust (diversification typically helps stabilize OOS Sharpe versus a single noisy signal). Given how it played out, the in-sample number is probably an optimistic upper bound rather than a reliable OOS estimate — hence the conservative prediction.
